title: An Eleven, a Ten, and the Trophy: Alex Baker Wins in Catalonia
title_candidates: An Eleven, a Ten, and the Trophy: Alex Baker Wins in Catalonia
106 and Still Eleven Clear: Alex Baker's TEG 18
Two Records at Camiral: Mullin's 84, Baker's 106
The Wreckage Was Immaterial: Alex Baker Takes TEG 18 by Eight
Spoon Holder Into Jacket, Champion Into Spoon
theme: Catalunya handed out an all-time TEG course record and an all-time course-worst in the same tournament, and the champion owned the worst one: Alex Baker banked points in bulk on the Tour and the Stadium and paid for his catastrophes in a currency the Trophy does not count. The recurring image is the double-figure hole — an 11, a 10, a 9, a string of 8s — carried through all four rounds as connective tissue. Treat the gross/Stableford split as comic accounting, not paradox: it is arithmetic, handled with a straight face, never a head-scratcher.
opening_hook: Open on Alex Baker walking off the 18th at the Tour course in R2 having signed for 106 — the worst gross round in 22 TEG visits to that course — and still leading the Trophy by 11, because on the only metric that counted the damage was already paid for.

trophy_storyline.subject: Alex Baker's Trophy: 169 points, two field-best rounds, and a course-worst gross that cost him nothing
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: Baker arrived with three prior Wooden Spoons and a Spoon in two of the last three TEGs, and won the Trophy by 8 while posting the worst gross round in 22 TEG visits to the Tour course.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: 46 points in R1, best in the field and 12 clear of Patterson, built on 17 points across holes 8-12 and 13 more over 14-16 (b40, b47); he led the Trophy at the end of every round (b37, b17, b05). Turn: the gross wreckage arrives — an 8 at the 16th in R2, a hole rated SI 17, then an 11 at the 18th, and a 106 that set a new Tour-course worst across 22 prior visits (b46, b36, cr02) — followed by a 10 at the 14th and an 8 at the 17th in R4 (b25, b43), and a fade from 2nd after R1 to 5th in the Jacket (b44). Resolution: on Stableford none of it registered beyond a zero — a field-best 44 in R3, anchored by 21 points over holes 11-16 (b04), restored the 12-point cushion, and a closing 38 was enough for 169 and an 8-point win (b01).

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams's Green Jacket: reigning Wooden Spoon holder to +66 and a 14-shot win
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Williams came in as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder from TEG 17 and won the Jacket outright by 14, beating Mullin head-to-head in three of the four rounds.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: a ruinous opening on the Tour — a 9 at the 7th, an 8 at the 17th (SI 3), 8 shots lost across holes 3-5 and a spell at the bottom of the Spoon race, arrested only by a birdie at the 15th (b24, b20, b31) — left him 27 over par and third. Turn: he answered with the best R2 in the field (b42), four straight gross pars over 13-16 worth 13 points (b19, b26), and took the Jacket lead outright at the 2nd hole of R3 (b28) once Jon Baker's 20-hole tenure in front ended (b48); he was never headed again (b17). Resolution: 13 over par in R3, then 12 over in R4 with a birdie at the 5th and 9 points across 8-10 (b10, b06) — an 84 at the Stadium, his personal best there by 8 — for +66 and the Jacket by 14 (b02).

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker's Wooden Spoon: the defending Trophy champion finishes 23 points adrift of the next man
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: He arrived as defending Trophy champion, led the Green Jacket inside the first five holes of the tournament, and still finished last on 126 points, 23 behind Mullin.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: Baker took the Jacket lead at the 5th in R1 and produced the tidiest golf anyone managed in R2 — five holes without dropping a gross shot, 16 points from the 14th to the 18th, birdie at the 14th — and still held the Jacket after two rounds (b09, b13, b37). Turn: he surrendered the Jacket lead to Williams at the 7th in R2 after 20 holes in front, retook it at the 9th, then gave it up for good at the 2nd hole of R3 (b48, b28) — the same hole at which he dropped to the bottom of the Spoon race and stayed there. Resolution: a 9 at the 4th in R3 (b39), 28 points that round and 29 in R4, last in the field in three of the four rounds, and the Spoon by 23 on 126 (b14).

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin: an 11 at the 15th, then the lowest gross round ever played at the Stadium
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The all-time TEG course record at PGA Catalunya - Stadium — 84 gross, beating 89 across 27 prior visits — came from the man who had been dumped to the bottom of the Spoon race by a single hole in R1.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 at the Tour course, the 15th, an 11 — sextuple bogey, no points — and in one hole he goes from 2nd to last in the Wooden Spoon race (b35, b66). Turn: moved onto the Stadium, the championship course of the two, he shoots 84 — a new all-time course record and his own personal best there by 7 (cr01). Resolution: with the Jacket still within reach he goes from the 14th to the 17th in R4 without a net par, bleeding 9 shots (b45, b49), and finishes runner-up in the Jacket by 14.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's second place, and the eight holes on the opening morning
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Patterson outscored the champion in two of the four rounds and still lost by 8, having gone 22 shots over par between the 3rd and the 10th of R1.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: an 8 at the 3rd in R1, then seven consecutive holes without a net par and 22 shots bled by the time he left the 10th green; he was bottom of the Spoon race by the 4th hole of the tournament (b23, b29, b18, b33). Turn: he spends the rest of the tournament hauling it back — 13 points across 13-16 to salvage R1, then 16 points over 11-15 in R2 despite another 8 at the 4th (SI 2) and 11 shots lost from the 6th to the 10th (b30, b11, b15, b32) — and sets personal bests at both courses along the way, 94 on the Tour in R2 and 93 at the Stadium in R3. Resolution: a birdie at the 17th in R4 halts one final slide (b03), and he finishes second, 8 adrift — a gap that had already been 12 before the first round was over.

vehicle_fit_response.note: The inventory is real — Alex Baker alone contributes four wreckage holes — but catalogue has led two of the last three reports; motif carries the same material as connective tissue instead, hung on the two all-time records (cr01, cr02) rather than listed out.

why_the_champion_won: A field-best 46 in R1 put him 12 clear before anyone had settled, a field-best 44 in R3 (21 points over holes 11-16) restored it, and he was the steadiest man in the field, never finishing a round worse than 3rd of 5 — while the only man in range, Patterson, had already spent 22 shots over eight holes on the opening morning; Patterson outscored him in two rounds and still lost by 8.
